config.title: Churches in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Which Berlin churches to go inside, what they cost, when they are open and how to fit them into one day.

items.q: Is the Berliner Dom free to enter?
items.a: No. A visit costs **EUR 15, reduced EUR 12**, with an audio guide included, and one adult ticket covers up to four children under 18. The ticket includes the Hohenzollern crypt, the museum and the dome walkway.

items.q: Which churches in Berlin are free to visit?
items.a: In the centre, **St. Marienkirche, St. Hedwig's Cathedral, the Friedrichswerdersche Kirche and the Parochialkirche** are free, and so is the new church of the **Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church** at Breitscheidplatz. The Berliner Dom (EUR 15) and the Nikolaikirche museum (EUR 7) charge entry.

items.q: What are the Berliner Dom opening hours?
items.a: **Monday to Saturday 9:00 to 18:00 and Sunday 12:00 to 18:00**, with last entry at 17:00. Services, concerts and events can change the hours on a given day, so check the Dom's own calendar that morning.

items.q: Can I visit Berlin churches on a Sunday?
items.a: Yes, but not in the morning. Services come first: the Berliner Dom opens to visitors at 12:00 and St. Hedwig's Cathedral at 13:00, and the Parochialkirche stays shut. **St. Marienkirche opens at 10:00**, which makes it the best Sunday start.

items.q: Is the Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church open?
items.a: The new blue-glass church is open **daily from 10:00 to 18:00**, free, except during services and concerts. The exhibition in the memorial hall of the old tower has been **closed for renovation since 29 August 2026**.

items.q: Which is the oldest church in Berlin?
items.a: The **Nikolaikirche** in the Nikolaiviertel is the oldest church building, now a museum. **St. Marienkirche** by the TV Tower is the oldest church still used for services.
